text: I think writing letters has its own very special value over texting and emails. And I don't want to romanticize it because emails and texts are just faster, more convenient, you can edit and correct, you can send to people all over the world. I don't want to romanticize the inconvenience of waiting for a letter. But when you write by hand, the care and attention you put into it, the time you put into it is really present in the letter. So you can see the unevenness of the letters, you can really see who wrote it. And it becomes a very intimate thing, a very slow, patient thing. And because it's slow and patient, you actually do pay attention to the letter. And because of that it becomes very meaningful and you really remember the little things. Plus, you can save a letter and re-read it many, many years later, while emails just get buried and disappear. So, it's a very meaningful thing.
